The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers:  While
we understand investors' concerns, in  Joe’s report , he indicated, “ In CY26 we think
that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities,
with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity ”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue  upside
from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the  AWS announcement ?  We
believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it
finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July. Some investors have
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for
Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect
Alchip. We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings
grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29. We reiterate our Tranium3
forecast  of  US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.  We suggest building positions

Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
•  Trainium3 UltraServer  –  Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering
4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2.
°  Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS,
customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times
°  Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and
Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%.
°  Decart is getting  4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the
cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads
•  Model workload  –    Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel
workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memory-
to-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
•  Memory  –    144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
•  Networking  –   Supportfor  both UALink and NVLink
°  According to Joe’s report  Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to
new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025) , "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion
caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental –  this will be
used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
•  Performance -  Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six
times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given
its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs ( link ). The future optical chiplet
selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a
partnership with Ayar Labs (see  SEMICON Taiwan takeaways ) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4. From our  Summit
Feedback , “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning
Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than
the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
No changes to our  Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying
1.2mn units in 2026. Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect
Trainium3 demand. Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We
remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud
AWS Trainium2:  Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service. We checked
current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream. This indicates 1.2mn
units on the upstream in 2025. For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3:  Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could
be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on
TSMC's 3nm supply. We expect higher production volumes from April  2026. We estimate
550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting  US$2.3bn in revenue, which
could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4:  Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can
continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see  link ).

Alchip's 2025 NT$ revenue could decline >35% YoY
We project a 37% Y/Y  decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier  strong TWD
appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm
crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.  US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the
company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline. We  expect Alchip's revenue to rebound
strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.

grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29. We reiterate our Tranium3

almost zero.  We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip;  at 20x our 2026e EPS we find

takeaways.

Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect 
Alchip. We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings 
grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29. We reiterate our Tranium3 
forecast  of  US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.  We suggest building positions 
on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in 
Trainium projects –  the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is 
almost zero.  We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip;  at 20x our 2026e EPS we find 
the stock attractive. Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key 
takeaways.

records.text: We project a 37% Y/Y decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier strong TWD appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.
records.raw_text:
We project a 37% Y/Y  decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier  strong TWD 
appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm 
crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.  US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the 
company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline. We  expect Alchip's revenue to rebound 
strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.

(as of November 30, 2025)
The Stock Ratings described below apply to Morgan Stanley's Fundamental Equity Research and do not apply to Debt Research produced by the Firm.
For disclosure purposes only (in accordance with FINRA requirements), we include the category headings of Buy, Hold, and Sell alongside our ratings of Overweight, Equal-weight, Not-Rated 
and Underweight. Morgan Stanley does not assign ratings of Buy, Hold or Sell to the stocks we cover. Overweight, Equal-weight, Not-Rated and Underweight are not the equivalent of buy, 
hold, and sell but represent recommended relative weightings (see definitions below). To satisfy regulatory requirements, we correspond Overweight, our most positive stock rating, with a 
buy recommendation; we correspond Equal-weight and Not-Rated to hold and Underweight to sell recommendations, respectively.

M
Idea
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
revenue weakness
AWS event takeaways
Trainium3 at re:Invent:
•  Trainium3 UltraServer  –  Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering
4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2.
°  Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS,
customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times
than Trainium2 UltraServers.
•  Focus on cost saving
°  Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and
Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%.
°  Decart is getting  4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the
cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads
on Trainium3.
•  Model workload  –    Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel
workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memory-
to-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
•  Memory  –    144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
Trainium4 at re:Invent:
•  Networking  –   Supportfor  both UALink and NVLink
°  According to Joe’s report  Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to
new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025) , "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion
caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental –  this will be
used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
•  Performance -  Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six
times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the
memory capacity.
Implications for Alchip
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given
its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs ( link ). The future optical chiplet
selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a
partnership with Ayar Labs (see  SEMICON Taiwan takeaways ) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4. From our  Summit
Feedback , “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning
Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than
the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.

We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given
its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs ( link ). The future optical chiplet
selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a
partnership with Ayar Labs (see  SEMICON Taiwan takeaways ) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4. From our  Summit
Feedback , “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning
Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than
the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.

M
Idea
No changes to our  Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent
CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying
1.2mn units in 2026. Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect
Trainium3 demand. Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We
remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud
provider." (See  link .)
AWS Trainium2:  Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service. We checked
current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream. This indicates 1.2mn
units on the upstream in 2025. For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3:  Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could
be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on
TSMC's 3nm supply. We expect higher production volumes from April  2026. We estimate
550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting  US$2.3bn in revenue, which
could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4:  Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can
continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see  link ).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp
in 2028.

STOCK RATINGS
Morgan Stanley uses a relative rating system using terms such as Overweight, Equal-weight, Not-Rated or Underweight (see definitions below). Morgan Stanley does not assign ratings of Buy,
Hold or Sell to the stocks we cover. Overweight, Equal-weight, Not-Rated and Underweight are not the equivalent of buy, hold and sell.  Investors should carefully read the definitions of all
ratings used in Morgan Stanley Research. In addition, since Morgan Stanley Research contains more complete information concerning the analyst's views, investors should carefully read Morgan
Stanley Research, in its entirety, and not infer the contents from the rating alone.  In any case, ratings (or research) should not be used or relied upon as investment advice.  An investor's decision
to buy or sell a stock should depend on individual circumstances (such as the investor's existing holdings) and other considerations.
Global Stock Ratings Distribution
(as of November 30, 2025)
The Stock Ratings described below apply to Morgan Stanley's Fundamental Equity Research and do not apply to Debt Research produced by the Firm.
For disclosure purposes only (in accordance with FINRA requirements), we include the category headings of Buy, Hold, and Sell alongside our ratings of Overweight, Equal-weight, Not-Rated
and Underweight. Morgan Stanley does not assign ratings of Buy, Hold or Sell to the stocks we cover. Overweight, Equal-weight, Not-Rated and Underweight are not the equivalent of buy,
hold, and sell but represent recommended relative weightings (see definitions below). To satisfy regulatory requirements, we correspond Overweight, our most positive stock rating, with a
buy recommendation; we correspond Equal-weight and Not-Rated to hold and Underweight to sell recommendations, respectively.

Alchip Technologies Ltd | Asia Pacific
Read-across from AWS re:Invent and Marvell results; keep OW
Trainium3's revenue contribution to Alchip should stay intact, while Alchip should be able to support both UALink and NVLink
for Trainium4.
Reiterate OW – accumulate on dips in particular.
Alchip stock was down 7% yesterday vs. the Taiex up 1%.
We cite two factors:
1.
Alchip plays a key role in design service for both the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chips.
There could have been profit-taking after AWS re:Invent yesterday, when the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chip architecture were announced.
2.
Key competitor Marvell (covered by Joe Moore) guided for ASIC business to grow in 2026.
Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in 2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.
The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue upside from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement?
We believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July.
Some investors have
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect Alchip.
We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29.
We reiterate our Tranium3 forecast of US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.
We suggest building positions on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in Trainium projects – the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is almost zero.
We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip; at 20x our 2026e EPS we find the stock attractive.
Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key takeaways.
M
Idea
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
revenue weakness
AWS event takeaways
Trainium3 at re:Invent:
• Trainium3 UltraServer – Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering 4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2. ° Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS, customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times than Trainium2 UltraServers.
• Focus on cost saving ° Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%. ° Decart is getting 4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads on Trainium3.
• Model workload – Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memoryto-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
• Memory – 144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
Trainium4 at re:Invent:
• Networking –Supportfor both UALink and NVLink ° According to Joe’s report Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025), "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental – this will be used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
• Performance - Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the memory capacity.
Implications for Alchip
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs (link).
The future optical chiplet selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a partnership with Ayar Labs (see SEMICON Taiwan takeaways) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4.
From our Summit Feedback, “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
2
M
Idea
No changes to our Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying 1.2mn units in 2026.
Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect Trainium3 demand.
Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud provider." (See link.)
AWS Trainium2: Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service.
We checked current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream.
This indicates 1.2mn units on the upstream in 2025.
For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3: Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on TSMC's 3nm supply.
We expect higher production volumes from April 2026.
We estimate 550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting US$2.3bn in revenue, which could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4: Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see link).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp in 2028.

Alchip's 2025 NT$ revenue could decline >35% YoY
We project a 37% Y/Y decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier strong TWD appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.
US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline.
We expect Alchip's revenue to rebound strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.
2026 looks strong with >100% Y/Y revenue growth, driven by:
• 3nm turnkey revenue ramp;
• Li Auto's 5nm project ramp-up; and
• Potential 2nm NRE revenue.
Other factors include some Japanese consumer ASIC projects and low production of AI ASIC from US AI start-ups.

Alchip Technologies Ltd | Asia Pacific
Read-across from AWS re:Invent and Marvell results; keep OW
Trainium3's revenue contribution to Alchip should stay intact, while Alchip should be able to support both UALink and NVLink
Reiterate OW – accumulate on dips in particular.
Alchip stock was down 7% yesterday vs. the Taiex up 1%.
Alchip plays a key role in design service for both the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chips.
There could have been profit-taking after AWS re:Invent yesterday, when the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chip architecture were announced.
Key competitor Marvell (covered by Joe Moore) guided for ASIC business to grow in 2026.
Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in 2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.

The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue upside from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement?
We believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July.
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect Alchip.
We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29.
We reiterate our Tranium3 forecast of US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.

We suggest building positions on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in Trainium projects – the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is almost zero.
We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip; at 20x our 2026e EPS we find the stock attractive.
Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key takeaways.
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
• Trainium3 UltraServer – Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering 4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2.
° Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS, customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times than Trainium2 UltraServers.
• Focus on cost saving ° Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%.
° Decart is getting 4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads on Trainium3.

• Model workload – Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memoryto-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
• Memory – 144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth

• Networking –Supportfor both UALink and NVLink ° According to Joe’s report Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025), "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental – this will be used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
• Performance - Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the memory capacity.
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs (link).
The future optical chiplet selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a partnership with Ayar Labs (see SEMICON Taiwan takeaways) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4.

From our Summit Feedback, “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
No changes to our Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying 1.2mn units in 2026.
Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect Trainium3 demand.
Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud provider." (See link.)
AWS Trainium2: Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service.
We checked current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream.
This indicates 1.2mn units on the upstream in 2025.
For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3: Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on TSMC's 3nm supply.
We expect higher production volumes from April 2026.
We estimate 550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting US$2.3bn in revenue, which could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4: Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see link).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp in 2028.

Alchip Technologies Ltd | Asia Pacific
Read-across from AWS re:Invent and Marvell results; keep OW
Trainium3's revenue contribution to Alchip should stay intact, while Alchip should be able to support both UALink and NVLink
for Trainium4.
Reiterate OW – accumulate on dips in particular.
Alchip stock was down 7% yesterday vs. the Taiex up 1%.
We cite two factors:
1.
Alchip plays a key role in design service for both the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chips.
There could have been profit-taking after AWS re:Invent yesterday, when the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chip architecture were announced.
2.
Key competitor Marvell (covered by Joe Moore) guided for ASIC business to grow in 2026.
Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in 2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.
The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue upside from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement?
We believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July.
Some investors have
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect Alchip.
We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29.
We reiterate our Tranium3 forecast of US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.
We suggest building positions on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in Trainium projects – the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is almost zero.
We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip; at 20x our 2026e EPS we find the stock attractive.
Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key takeaways.
M
Idea
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
revenue weakness
AWS event takeaways
Trainium3 at re:Invent:
• Trainium3 UltraServer – Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering 4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2. ° Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS, customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times than Trainium2 UltraServers.
• Focus on cost saving ° Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%. ° Decart is getting 4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads on Trainium3.
• Model workload – Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memoryto-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
• Memory – 144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
Trainium4 at re:Invent:
• Networking –Supportfor both UALink and NVLink ° According to Joe’s report Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025), "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental – this will be used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
• Performance - Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the memory capacity.
Implications for Alchip
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs (link).
The future optical chiplet selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a partnership with Ayar Labs (see SEMICON Taiwan takeaways) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4.
From our Summit Feedback, “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
2
M
Idea
No changes to our Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying 1.2mn units in 2026.
Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect Trainium3 demand.
Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud provider." (See link.)
AWS Trainium2: Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service.
We checked current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream.
This indicates 1.2mn units on the upstream in 2025.
For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3: Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on TSMC's 3nm supply.
We expect higher production volumes from April 2026.
We estimate 550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting US$2.3bn in revenue, which could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4: Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see link).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp in 2028.

Alchip's 2025 NT$ revenue could decline >35% YoY
We project a 37% Y/Y decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier strong TWD appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.
US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline.
We expect Alchip's revenue to rebound strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.
2026 looks strong with >100% Y/Y revenue growth, driven by:
• 3nm turnkey revenue ramp;
• Li Auto's 5nm project ramp-up; and
• Potential 2nm NRE revenue.
Other factors include some Japanese consumer ASIC projects and low production of AI ASIC from US AI start-ups.

Alchip Technologies Ltd | Asia Pacific
Read-across from AWS re:Invent and Marvell results; keep OW
Trainium3's revenue contribution to Alchip should stay intact, while Alchip should be able to support both UALink and NVLink
for Trainium4.
Reiterate OW – accumulate on dips in particular.
Alchip stock was down 7% yesterday vs. the Taiex up 1%.
We cite two factors:
1.
Alchip plays a key role in design service for both the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chips.
There could have been profit-taking after AWS re:Invent yesterday, when the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chip architecture were announced.
2.
Key competitor Marvell (covered by Joe Moore) guided for ASIC business to grow in 2026.
Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in 2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.
The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue upside from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement?
We believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July.
Some investors have
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect Alchip.
We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29.
We reiterate our Tranium3 forecast of US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.
We suggest building positions on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in Trainium projects – the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is almost zero.
We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip; at 20x our 2026e EPS we find the stock attractive.
Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key takeaways.
M
Idea
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
revenue weakness
AWS event takeaways
Trainium3 at re:Invent:
• Trainium3 UltraServer – Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering 4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2. ° Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS, customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times than Trainium2 UltraServers.
• Focus on cost saving ° Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%. ° Decart is getting 4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads on Trainium3.
• Model workload – Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memoryto-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
• Memory – 144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
Trainium4 at re:Invent:
• Networking –Supportfor both UALink and NVLink ° According to Joe’s report Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025), "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental – this will be used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
• Performance - Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the memory capacity.
Implications for Alchip
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs (link).
The future optical chiplet selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a partnership with Ayar Labs (see SEMICON Taiwan takeaways) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4.
From our Summit Feedback, “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
2
M
Idea
No changes to our Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying 1.2mn units in 2026.
Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect Trainium3 demand.
Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud provider." (See link.)
AWS Trainium2: Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service.
We checked current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream.
This indicates 1.2mn units on the upstream in 2025.
For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3: Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on TSMC's 3nm supply.
We expect higher production volumes from April 2026.
We estimate 550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting US$2.3bn in revenue, which could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4: Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see link).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp in 2028.

Alchip's 2025 NT$ revenue could decline >35% YoY
We project a 37% Y/Y decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier strong TWD appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.
US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline.
We expect Alchip's revenue to rebound strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.
2026 looks strong with >100% Y/Y revenue growth, driven by:
• 3nm turnkey revenue ramp;
• Li Auto's 5nm project ramp-up; and
• Potential 2nm NRE revenue.
Other factors include some Japanese consumer ASIC projects and low production of AI ASIC from US AI start-ups.

repair.original_text:
Alchip Technologies Ltd | Asia Pacific
Read-across from AWS re:Invent and Marvell results; keep OW
Trainium3's revenue contribution to Alchip should stay intact, while Alchip should be able to support both UALink and NVLink
for Trainium4.
Reiterate OW – accumulate on dips in particular.
Alchip stock was down 7% yesterday vs. the Taiex up 1%.
We cite two factors:
1.
Alchip plays a key role in design service for both the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chips.
There could have been profit-taking after AWS re:Invent yesterday, when the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chip architecture were announced.
2.
Key competitor Marvell (covered by Joe Moore) guided for ASIC business to grow in 2026.
Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in 2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.
The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue upside from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement?
We believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July.
Some investors have
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect Alchip.
We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29.
We reiterate our Tranium3 forecast of US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.
We suggest building positions on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in Trainium projects – the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is almost zero.
We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip; at 20x our 2026e EPS we find the stock attractive.
Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key takeaways.
M
Idea
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
revenue weakness
AWS event takeaways
Trainium3 at re:Invent:
• Trainium3 UltraServer – Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering 4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2. ° Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS, customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times than Trainium2 UltraServers.
• Focus on cost saving ° Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%. ° Decart is getting 4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads on Trainium3.
• Model workload – Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memoryto-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
• Memory – 144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
Trainium4 at re:Invent:
• Networking –Supportfor both UALink and NVLink ° According to Joe’s report Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025), "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental – this will be used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
• Performance - Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the memory capacity.
Implications for Alchip
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs (link).
The future optical chiplet selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a partnership with Ayar Labs (see SEMICON Taiwan takeaways) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4.
From our Summit Feedback, “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
2
M
Idea
No changes to our Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying 1.2mn units in 2026.
Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect Trainium3 demand.
Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud provider." (See link.)
AWS Trainium2: Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service.
We checked current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream.
This indicates 1.2mn units on the upstream in 2025.
For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3: Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on TSMC's 3nm supply.
We expect higher production volumes from April 2026.
We estimate 550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting US$2.3bn in revenue, which could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4: Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see link).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp in 2028.

Alchip's 2025 NT$ revenue could decline >35% YoY
We project a 37% Y/Y decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier strong TWD appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.
US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline.
We expect Alchip's revenue to rebound strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.
2026 looks strong with >100% Y/Y revenue growth, driven by:
• 3nm turnkey revenue ramp;
• Li Auto's 5nm project ramp-up; and
• Potential 2nm NRE revenue.
Other factors include some Japanese consumer ASIC projects and low production of AI ASIC from US AI start-ups.

Alchip Technologies Ltd | Asia Pacific
Read-across from AWS re:Invent and Marvell results; keep OW
Trainium3's revenue contribution to Alchip should stay intact, while Alchip should be able to support both UALink and NVLink
for Trainium4.
Reiterate OW – accumulate on dips in particular.
Alchip stock was down 7% yesterday vs. the Taiex up 1%.
We cite two factors:
1.
Alchip plays a key role in design service for both the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chips.
There could have been profit-taking after AWS re:Invent yesterday, when the Trainium3 system and Trainium4 chip architecture were announced.
2.
Key competitor Marvell (covered by Joe Moore) guided for ASIC business to grow in 2026.
Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in 2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.
The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”.
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue upside from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle.
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement?
We believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July.
Some investors have
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect Alchip.
We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29.
We reiterate our Tranium3 forecast of US$2.3bn in 2026 and US$3.3bn in 2027.
We suggest building positions on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in Trainium projects – the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is almost zero.
We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip; at 20x our 2026e EPS we find the stock attractive.
Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key takeaways.

Idea
Alchip's 3nm project shows upside, offsetting near-term
revenue weakness
AWS event takeaways
Trainium3 at re:Invent:
• Trainium3 UltraServer – Up to 144 Trainium3 chips in a single system, delivering 4.4x more computing performance and 4x better energy efficiency than Trainium2. ° Testing Trainium3 UltraServers with OpenAI's open weight model GPT-OSS, customers can get 3x higher throughput per chip and 4x faster response times than Trainium2 UltraServers.
• Focus on cost saving ° Customers including Anthropic, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI, Ricoh, and Splash Music are reducing training and inference costs by up to 50%. ° Decart is getting 4x faster inference for real-time generative video at half the cost of GPUs, and Amazon Bedrock is already running production workloads on Trainium3.
• Model workload – Trainium3 is designed for both dense and expert-parallel workloads with advanced data types (MXFP8 and MXFP4) and improved memoryto-computing balance for real-time, multi-modal, and reasoning tasks.
• Memory – 144 GB of HBM3e memory and 4.9 TB/s of memory bandwidth
Trainium4 at re:Invent:
• Networking –Supportfor both UALink and NVLink ° According to Joe’s report Astera Labs Inc: AWS Trainium 4 unveiling points to new ALAB opportunities (3 Dec 2025), "Amazon's use of NVLink Fusion caused a tailspin in Astera Labs, but it is actually incremental – this will be used in hybrid racks with both GPU and Trainium 4.
• Performance - Compared to Trainium 3, the next generation chip will deliver six times the FP4 performance, 4 times the memory bandwidth and two times the memory capacity.
Implications for Alchip
We believe Alchip is also the only design service provider for the electrical I/O die, given its strong partnerships with Synopsys and Astera Labs (link).
The future optical chiplet selection remains to be seen if/when Trainium enters CPO, but Alchip has formed a partnership with Ayar Labs (see SEMICON Taiwan takeaways) to compete.
We still believe Alchip is the only design service provider for Trainium4.
From our Summit Feedback, “Alchip seeks a ‘win-win’ situation with the major customer at 2nm, meaning Alchip’s revenue and profits can grow with the customer’s demand, at least better than the 3nm generation, given Alchip’s value-added to this complex 2nm design.
2
M
Idea
No changes to our Trainium3 chip forecasts after our recent CoWoS model updates
Our industry checks show no change to AWS Trainium3 CoWoS allocation, still implying 1.2mn units in 2026.
Investors asked whether Anthropic adopting TPU would affect Trainium3 demand.
Anthropic's press release names AWS as its main cloud provider: "We remain committed to our partnership with Amazon, our primary training partner and cloud provider." (See link.)
AWS Trainium2: Marvell handles the 5nm AWS Trainium2 design service.
We checked current Trainium2 volumes in Asia across upstream and downstream.
This indicates 1.2mn units on the upstream in 2025.
For 2026, we assume T2 volumes fall to 320k units.
AWS Trainium3: Our Asian supply chain checks suggest that Trainium3 chip volume could be somewhere between 1.2mn to 1.8mn units in 2026, with the upside depending on TSMC's 3nm supply.
We expect higher production volumes from April 2026.
We estimate 550-600k Trainium3 chips for Alchip in 2026, suggesting US$2.3bn in revenue, which could further increase to US$3.3bn in 2027.
AWS Trainium4: Our Asian Semi team also thinks it is highly likely that Alchip can continue to win 2nm given lower cost, better service, and third-party IP support (see link).
We assume that Trainium4 enters small production in late 2027, followed by a fast ramp in 2028.

Alchip's 2025 NT$ revenue could decline >35% YoY
We project a 37% Y/Y decline in 2025 NT$ revenue, reflecting earlier strong TWD appreciation against US$ and several projects delays or de-commitments, including 3nm crypto, Li Auto, and Habana.
US$-denominated revenue could decline 35% Y/Y, missing the company's guidance of a 10-20% Y/Y decline.
We expect Alchip's revenue to rebound strongly in 2026 with Trainium3 and Li Auto contribution.
2026 looks strong with >100% Y/Y revenue growth, driven by:
• 3nm turnkey revenue ramp;
• Li Auto's 5nm project ramp-up; and
• Potential 2nm NRE revenue.
Other factors include some Japanese consumer ASIC projects and low production of AI ASIC from US AI start-ups.
